title: Quoting Fundamentals knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Quoting Fundamentals”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Why quoting matters” under lesson 21, “Quoting Fundamentals”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Quoting Fundamentals”?
options: Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
questions.answer_key: Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution.
questions.explanation: Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Quoting Fundamentals”?
options: Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Preserve values as separate arguments, quote expansions, and test inputs containing spaces or special characters.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
questions.answer_key: Preserve values as separate arguments, quote expansions, and test inputs containing spaces or special characters.
questions.explanation: Preserve values as separate arguments, quote expansions, and test inputs containing spaces or special characters. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
